delay.description: How long the pointer must rest on the control before the tip appears, in milliseconds. Keyboard focus never waits: a reader who tabbed to the control has already committed. Read only on the FALLBACK path — where the engine implements interest invokers and the control carries interestfor, the wait is the platform's own interest-delay-start and this number is not consulted, so set the CSS property on the control if you need to change it there.

for.description: The id of the control this tip describes, in the same root. The declarative wiring is the other way round and is preferred — interestfor on the control, naming this tip's id, and this prop left unset — and it works on every engine: where interest invokers are missing the tip binds an interestfor control's pointer and focus events itself, exactly as it does for a control this prop names. Either way the listeners come off again when the tip leaves the document. It is read once, at mount; a host that wires a tip up later calls bindTooltip from jx-ui:/behaviors/tooltip.ts itself.

x.description: Where the tip's inline-start edge sits, in viewport pixels. Written by the element when it opens, from the box of the control it describes; a host that places the tip itself sets it and names no control.

y.description: Where the tip's block-start edge sits, in viewport pixels. The tip is placed under its control, or above it when there is no room below — never over it, because a tip that covers the control it describes hides what the reader is pointing at.

arrow.description: Draws a pointer at the edge of the tip that faces its control — the block-start edge for a tip below it, the block-end edge for one that flipped above. Decorative, and aria-hidden: it says nothing the tip's own text does not.

flipped.description: Whether the tip landed ABOVE its control because there was no room below. Written by the element when it opens, and read by nothing but the arrow: a pointer pinned to the block-start edge of a tip that flipped points away from the control it belongs to. A host that places the tip itself sets x and y, and sets this to say which way its arrow faces.

open.description: Whether the tip is showing. Follows the platform's toggle event; write it through showPopover() and hidePopover(), not directly.

onToggle.description: Mirrors the platform's toggle into open, and places a freshly shown tip under the control it describes. Placing here rather than on the gesture is what lets the declarative path work: an interestfor control shows the tip without telling the element anything, and the toggle is the first the element hears of it.

onReady.description: Binds the control the tip is wired to — the one for names, or the one declaring interestfor at this tip — on the fallback path. Nothing is bound where the engine implements interest invokers and the control declares one, because there the platform owns the pair.

onUnmount.description: Takes the fallback listeners off the control again. They sit on an element the kit does not own and which outlives the tip, so without this a removed tip keeps answering its control's pointer.

onMount.description: Announces that the element has rendered and carries its popover attribute, so a host may show it — and gives the element its own first sight of itself, which is how onReady reaches the control that for names.

style.transition: opacity var(--jx-dur-1) var(--jx-ease-out), display var(--jx-dur-1) allow-discrete, overlay var(--jx-dur-1) allow-discrete
